text: Ronnestad and colleagues (190) carried out a similar within-subject design as that of West and colleagues (246), except that the high-hormone group performed lower-body exercise before elbow flexion exercise. In contrast to the findings of West and colleagues (246), significantly greater increases in elbow flexor cross-sectional area were noted in the high-hormone condition, implying a causal link between acute hormonal elevations and hypertrophic adaptations. Differences were region specific, and increases in cross-sectional area were seen only at the two middle sections of the elbow flexors where muscle girth was largest.
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
chapter: Chapter 1: Hypertrophy-Related Responses and Adaptations to Exercise Stress
